cultural.vision_reason: The description explicitly identifies this as "Chian Grand Style" pottery depicting a chiton and himation (Greek/Chiot garment terms), a Greek ceramic tradition with black-figure-style banding — this is ancient Greek pottery, unrelated to Khmer ceramics.

physical.title: chalice
physical.summary: Body sherd of Chian Grand Style pottery chalice; creamy white slip; interior: glazed black (mostly worn) with traces of one added red band and traces of added white below; exterior: painted decoration consisting of wavy pale brown lines of chiton and part of black himation with border of staggered black dots between brown lines; ancient repair hole.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a chipped sherd fragment from a stamped pottery vessel, decorated with a stag motif in a stamped roundel — plausible ancient earthenware from the Khmer/Southeast Asian archaeological record.

physical.title: jar
physical.summary: Pottery jar; sandy yellowish brown fabric; probably coil-built, with lightly undulating interior; exterior decorated with a large circular stamp consisting of a stag standing facing right (as impressed) and enclosed within a saw-tooth border; a row of hollow circular impressions impressed immediately below; secondary chipping of the edges to create an approximately circular sherd.

cultural.vision_reason: This is an Andean (Inca/Chimú-style) blackware paccha/vessel combining an aríbalo chamber with a chaquitaclla (foot-plough) spout, per the museum's own description — a Peruvian ceramic form, not Cambodian/Khmer.

physical.title: vessel; paccha
physical.summary: Paccha; vessel.  Upper chamber is an aribola with flaring flat-rimmed spout and strap handles low down on sides; surmounts a chaquitaclla or Andean foot plough.  Two sets of vertical moulds used - one for aribalus (seams down sides) and the other for the chaquitaclla (seams along top and bottom).  Well-burnished.  Black. Also called wirki considering its form (see the hol on the bottom).
